title: State Entropy Regularization for Robust Reinforcement Learning

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines reward uncertainty sets with the condition '~r ≯ r' (i.e., ~r(s,a) ≤ r(s,a) for some state-action pair) to ensure the adversary degrades performance. However, Theorem 3.1 omits this condition, and the derived adversarial reward ~r(s,a) = r(s,a) - α log d_P^π(s) - ε can exceed r(s,a) when d_P^π(s) is small, violating the intended uncertainty set. The same issue affects the policy entropy and state-action entropy results in Table 1, invalidating the claimed duality between entropy-regularized objectives and the described robust RL problems.

Theorem 3.3 is not stated as a precise mathematical formula; instead it is a verbal description: 'an approximate lower bound ... can be characterized ... under restrictive assumptions ...'. A theorem must include a clear mathematical statement. The absence of a formal inequality makes the claimed result unverifiable and the theorem empty.

The theorem lacks a definition of 'the robust return condition' and the proof is insufficient. The argument assumes, without clarification, that the regularized objective must equal the robust return, and uses a trivially constant-reward MDP to derive a contradiction that shows nothing beyond the fact that a nonzero regularizer cannot equal the nominal return in that trivial case. This does not support the strong claim that entropy regularization cannot solve kernel robust RL problems in general.

The text refers to Figure 5(b) for the rollouts ablation ('Figure 5(b) shows that with very limited rollouts...') and to Figure 5(c) for the regularization strength experiment. However, in the actual figure panel layout, (b) is 'Reward Shift', (c) is 'Rollouts Per Entropy Estimation Ablation', and (d) is 'Varying Regularization Strengths'. The mismatched references mislead the reader about which data is being discussed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5, paragraph 'Transition kernel robustness via entropy regularization' and Introduction
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference [6] (Chen et al., 2019, 'Top-K off-policy correction for a REINFORCE recommender system') is cited as the source of the PR-MDP and NR-MDP frameworks used as robustness baselines, but that paper is about recommender systems and has no relation to robust MDP frameworks. This is a critical miscitation. Additionally, in the Introduction, the same reference [6] is cited to support the claim of RL success across 'synthetic domains', which is also incorrect.

The document contains multiple extraneous image placeholders with captions such as 'Preliminaries, index 7', 'Method, index 18', and 'Experiments, index 29', which are not referenced in the text and do not correspond to any meaningful content. These artifacts indicate a corrupted or unedited manuscript, undermining the paper's presentation.
